# Frontend UI Engineering

## Overview

Build production-quality user interfaces that are accessible, performant, and visually polished. The goal is UI that looks like it was built by a design-aware engineer at a top company — not like it was generated by an AI. This means real design system adherence, proper accessibility, thoughtful interaction patterns, and no generic "AI aesthetic."

## When to Use

- Building new UI components or pages
- Modifying existing user-facing interfaces
- Implementing responsive layouts
- Adding interactivity or state management
- Fixing visual or UX issues

## Verify With What the Project Has

Run the project's own test, type-check, or lint commands. Don't install a framework, test runner, or type checker just to check your work; if the project has none, review the code against the [Verification](#verification) list and say what you could not run.

## Component Architecture

### File Structure

Colocate everything related to a component:

```
src/components/
  TaskList/
    TaskList.tsx          # Component implementation
    TaskList.test.tsx     # Tests
    TaskList.stories.tsx  # Storybook stories (if using)
    use-task-list.ts      # Custom hook (if complex state)
    types.ts              # Component-specific types (if needed)
```

### Component Patterns

**Prefer composition over configuration:**

```tsx
// Good: Composable
<Card>
  <CardHeader>
    <CardTitle>Tasks</CardTitle>
  </CardHeader>
  <CardBody>
    <TaskList tasks={tasks} />
  </CardBody>
</Card>

// Avoid: Over-configured
<Card
  title="Tasks"
  headerVariant="large"
  bodyPadding="md"
  content={<TaskList tasks={tasks} />}
/>
```

**Keep components focused:**

```tsx
// Good: Does one thing
export function TaskItem({ task, onToggle, onDelete }: TaskItemProps) {
  return (
    <li className="flex items-center gap-3 p-3">
      <Checkbox checked={task.done} onChange={() => onToggle(task.id)} />
      <span className={task.done ? 'line-through text-muted' : ''}>{task.title}</span>
      <Button variant="ghost" size="sm" onClick={() => onDelete(task.id)}>
        <TrashIcon />
      </Button>
    </li>
  );
}
```

**Separate data fetching from presentation:**

```tsx
// Container: handles data
export function TaskListContainer() {
  const { tasks, isLoading, error, refetch, toggleTask, deleteTask } = useTasks();

  if (isLoading) return <TaskListSkeleton />;
  if (error) return <ErrorState message="Failed to load tasks" retry={refetch} />;
  if (tasks.length === 0) return <EmptyState message="No tasks yet" />;

  return <TaskList tasks={tasks} onToggle={toggleTask} onDelete={deleteTask} />;
}

// Presentation: handles rendering
export function TaskList({ tasks, onToggle, onDelete }: { tasks: Task[] } & Pick<TaskItemProps, 'onToggle' | 'onDelete'>) {
  return (
    <ul role="list" className="divide-y">
      {tasks.map(task => <TaskItem key={task.id} task={task} onToggle={onToggle} onDelete={onDelete} />)}
    </ul>
  );
}
```

## State Management

**Choose the simplest approach that works:**

```
Local state (useState)           → Component-specific UI state
Lifted state                     → Shared between 2-3 sibling components
Context                          → Theme, auth, locale (read-heavy, write-rare)
URL state (searchParams)         → Filters, pagination, shareable UI state
Server state (React Query, SWR)  → Remote data with caching
Global store (Zustand, Redux)    → Complex client state shared app-wide
```

**Avoid prop drilling deeper than 3 levels.** If you're passing props through components that don't use them, introduce context or restructure the component tree.

# Accessibility (a11y)

Comprehensive accessibility guidelines based on WCAG 2.2 and Lighthouse accessibility audits. Goal: make content usable by everyone, including people with disabilities.

## Evidence-led audit workflow

When a rendered page is available:

1. Run a live Lighthouse Accessibility audit when that capability is available; with Chrome DevTools MCP, use `lighthouse_audit`. Use mobile navigation mode for a general public page or snapshot mode when reloading would lose authenticated or user-created state.
2. Use failed audit nodes to localize the relevant component or template instead of searching the whole repository for generic patterns.
3. Inspect a rendered accessibility-tree snapshot for names, roles, states, landmarks, and heading structure; with Chrome DevTools MCP, use `take_snapshot`. Exercise the affected flow with the keyboard.
4. Fix the source, then re-run the same audit and manual interaction.

If the live tools are unavailable, use Lighthouse CLI or axe for automated coverage and complete the same manual checks. Automated tools detect only a subset of accessibility barriers: a score of 100 is not WCAG conformance, and a low score does not replace issue-level evidence.

## WCAG Principles: POUR

| Principle | Description |
|-----------|-------------|
| **P**erceivable | Content can be perceived through different senses |
| **O**perable | Interface can be operated by all users |
| **U**nderstandable | Content and interface are understandable |
| **R**obust | Content works with assistive technologies |

## Conformance levels

| Level | Requirement | Target |
|-------|-------------|--------|
| **A** | Minimum accessibility | Must pass |
| **AA** | Standard compliance | Should pass (legal requirement in many jurisdictions) |
| **AAA** | Enhanced accessibility | Nice to have |

---

## Perceivable

### Text alternatives (1.1)

**Images require alt text:**
```html
<!-- ❌ Missing alt -->
<img src="chart.png">

<!-- ✅ Descriptive alt -->
<img src="chart.png" alt="Bar chart showing 40% increase in Q3 sales">

<!-- ✅ Decorative image (empty alt) -->
<img src="decorative-border.png" alt="" role="presentation">

<!-- ✅ Complex image with longer description -->
<figure>
  <img src="infographic.png" alt="2024 market trends infographic" 
       aria-describedby="infographic-desc">
  <figcaption id="infographic-desc">
    <!-- Detailed description -->
  </figcaption>
</figure>
```

**Icon buttons need accessible names:**
```html
<!-- ❌ No accessible name -->
<button><svg><!-- menu icon --></svg></button>

<!-- ✅ Using aria-label -->
<button aria-label="Open menu">
  <svg aria-hidden="true"><!-- menu icon --></svg>
</button>

<!-- ✅ Using visually hidden text -->
<button>
  <svg aria-hidden="true"><!-- menu icon --></svg>
  <span class="visually-hidden">Open menu</span>
</button>
```

**Visually hidden class:**
```css
.visually-hidden {
  position: absolute;
  width: 1px;
  height: 1px;
  padding: 0;
  margin: -1px;
  overflow: hidden;
  clip: rect(0, 0, 0, 0);
  white-space: nowrap;
  border: 0;
}
```

| Text Size | AA minimum | AAA enhanced |
|-----------|------------|--------------|
| Normal text (< 18px / < 14px bold) | 4.5:1 | 7:1 |
| Large text (≥ 18px / ≥ 14px bold) | 3:1 | 4.5:1 |
| UI components & graphics | 3:1 | 3:1 |

# Auto insurance quote design system

**Status** Human approved on 2026-11-22 ([approval record](../approvals/US-01-design-approval.md))  
**Scope** US-01 and a shared visual language for later wizard steps  
**Approved inputs** [US-01](../../spec/US-01.md), [technology stack](../architecture/US-01-technology-stack.md), [country routing](../adr/ADR-001-multi-country-content.md), [dynamic form](../adr/ADR-002-dynamic-form-contract.md), and [wizard state](../adr/ADR-003-frontend-quote-state.md)

## Direction

A driver should be able to tell which country governs the quote, what information to supply, and what they can do next. Treat each step as part of one readable quote document. The global header carries the product identity. The progress track leads directly into the step content. On desktop, center the track and the active step composition. The country picker and URL establish the country, and each step shows the relevant business content for that country. Price and quote reference get strong typographic emphasis where they become a purchase decision or receipt.

White policy paper, pale blue tint, dark ink and the red print of a correction inform the palette. Use flat layers, simple document rules, and a single blue primary action. Georgia gives screen titles and milestones the rhythm of a document. Platform sans-serif keeps labels, entry fields and values easy to scan. The visual language is shared. Actual terminology and business content identify each country.

The review and plan patterns draw on GOV.UK's check-answers design and native radio grouping, with step-specific edit links and prices next to plan choices. [GOV.UK check answers](https://design-system.service.gov.uk/patterns/check-answers/), [GOV.UK radios](https://design-system.service.gov.uk/components/radios/)

## Foundations

Map the proposed tokens to the approved Tailwind CSS 4 theme during implementation. Use the colors on opaque surfaces.

| Token | Value and use |
| --- | --- |
| `surface-canvas` | `#F5F7FC` · background |
| `surface-panel` | `#FFFFFF` · controls, cards, header and focus gap |
| `surface-context` | `#EAF0FF` · selected plan and price block |
| `text-primary` | `#15243B` · headings, labels and values |
| `text-secondary` | `#344763` · explanatory copy |
| `text-muted` | `#405575` · help, placeholders and inactive progress labels |
| `action-primary` | `#2E6DF6` · primary and current-step fills with white foreground |
| `action-hover` | `#215BCC` · hovered or pressed primary fill |
| `action-inline` | `#1748AF` · inline links, emphasized blue text, and selected borders |
| `border-control` | `#586D91` · input, radio and checkbox outlines |
| `border-divider` | `#CCD8EE` · decorative rules |
| `focus-ring` | `#1746B4` · 2 px keyboard outline with 2 px offset. Preserve a white gap around saturated controls. |
| `intent-error` / `surface-error` | `#9E2F26` / `#FFF2EF` · invalid control, error text and recoverable panel |
| `intent-success` / `surface-success` | `#1F5B39` / `#E8F5EC` · success wording and icon |
| `surface-disabled` | `#E0E7F4` · disabled payment before consent and during processing |

| Foreground and background | Calculated contrast |
| --- | --- |
| Primary text on paper / canvas | 15.59:1 / 14.54:1 |
| Secondary text on paper / canvas | 9.43:1 / 8.80:1 |
| Muted text on paper / canvas / disabled fill | 7.57:1 / 7.06:1 / 6.09:1 |
| White text on primary / hovered primary | 4.53:1 / 6.12:1 |
| Inline action on paper / canvas / context tint | 8.13:1 / 7.59:1 / 7.13:1 |
| Control outline on paper / canvas | 5.24:1 / 4.88:1 |
| Focus outline on paper / canvas / context tint | 8.17:1 / 7.62:1 / 7.16:1 |
| Error on paper / error tint | 7.27:1 / 6.65:1 |
| Success on success tint | 7.16:1 |

Contrast uses WCAG relative luminance. Normal text targets at least 4.5:1 and essential control outlines or state indicators at least 3:1 against their surroundings. Use opaque primary blue with a white foreground and the darker inline blue for text on tinted surfaces. Messages and checked states carry meaning alongside color. [Text contrast](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/contrast-minimum.html), [Non-text contrast](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/non-text-contrast.html)

| Scale | Proposed use |
| --- | --- |
| Page title | Georgia 48/56 px wide, 32/40 px compact, normal weight |
| Section title | Georgia 28/36 px wide, 22/30 px compact, normal weight |
| Receipt number or price | System sans 28/36 px, 700, tabular numerals |
| Default body / input | System sans 16/24 px, 400 |
| Control label / button | System sans 15/20 px, 700, sentence case |
| Help / inline feedback | System sans 14/20 px, 400 for help and 700 for feedback |
| Spacing | 4, 8, 12, 16, 20, 24, 32, 40, 48 and 56 px. Use 8 px within a field, 20–24 px between fields, and 32–48 px between surfaces. |
| Shapes | 6 px controls, 8 px panels, 10 px receipt. Use tonal layers and borders. |
| Targets | At least 44 px for controls and padded link hit zones. The primary action is 48 px high. |
| Motion | At most 120 ms on fill or border changes. Reduced motion uses instant states and a static loading cue. |

## Layout and order

| Viewport | Layout |
| --- | --- |
| Compact, below 48 rem | Four-column shell with 16–20 px side padding. Fields span the content in published order. Use a compact three-label progress row. Allow copy to grow vertically. |
| Medium, 48–63.99 rem | Center one main flow. Pair consecutive fields where each gets at least 16 rem. Ancillary content follows its related block. |
| Wide, from 64 rem | Center the progress track, titles, and active step. Cap the main form and plan lane at 44.5 rem. Use a centered 58 rem composition for the summary’s paired review and price panels. Keep fields and reading text aligned to the start of their lanes. Fill the two form tracks row by row in DOM order. |

Keep the same reading order at every width and country. Labels, help, validation messages, prices and country links need room to wrap. Keep focus and errors fully visible. Verify vertical reflow at 320 CSS px and 400% zoom. The 390 px and 1200 px wireframes are review samples. [WCAG reflow](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/reflow.html), [WCAG target size](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/target-size-minimum.html)

## Components and states

| Pattern | Design contract |
| --- | --- |
| Header and country selection | The global header shows product identity. The picker and recovery for unsupported routes offer links to supported countries. The URL sets the active country and its isolated quote state. Include a main landmark, skip link and unique heading. On wizard navigation, focus the new screen heading. |
| Progress track | An informational ordered list of Datos, Plan and Resumen, centered on desktop. Mark the current step with `aria-current="step"` and expose completed status as text to assistive technology. Use separate Back and Edit actions. |
| Field | Use a visible programmatically associated label. Explain the required marker and expose requiredness natively. Use native inputs, select and checkbox. Associate help and the visible error with stable `aria-describedby` IDs. |
| Field feedback | Neutral on initial render. Show the configured error on invalid blur or unsuccessful Continue. Update or clear it as touched values change. Set `aria-invalid` while showing the error and move focus to the first invalid field on Continue. |
| Required select | Start on an unselectable placeholder with valid options waiting for a choice. After blur or Continue, show the configured required error. A required select without valid options uses the unavailable-form state. |
| Buttons and links | Buttons handle Continue, Retry and Simulate. Links handle Back and Edit. Continue remains operable in a ready invalid form. Payment is disabled before consent and during processing, with an adjacent explanation or status. |
| Loading and failure | Announce a concise polite status during retrieval. Use decorative placeholders while reading configuration for the active URL country. For missing, invalid, or failed configuration, replace the fields with a recoverable message and retry. |
| Plans | Later concept uses a native radio group with a visible legend. Recommendation and checked status have separate indicators. Keep local price, coverage and benefits close to the option. |
| Summary and receipt | Later concept uses a readable definition list and contextual edit links. Apply partial document masking to visible and spoken values. Terms and consent precede payment. Success wording accompanies a selectable quote reference. |
| Icons | Use individual local Tabler SVGs with the upstream notice. Decorative icons stay hidden from assistive technology. The shield in these frames is schematic. |

Use Spanish as the demo shell language. Keep the design notes in English and change local language attributes only for content that needs them. No static example substitutes for published Strapi business copy. [WCAG 2.2](https://www.w3.org/TR/WCAG22/), [W3C form notifications](https://www.w3.org/WAI/tutorials/forms/notifications/)

## Review and verification

The design check covers contrast, SVG accessible names, hierarchy, reading order and example wrapping. At implementation, verify both countries with keyboard and screen reader, invalid Continue, long Strapi fixtures, retry announcement, zoom, touch bounds and visible focus. Use automated accessibility checks and browser assertions alongside manual assistive-technology testing. [Wireframes and criteria map](US-01-wireframes.md)

The review draft incorporates the requested centered desktop steps and primary blue. Country selection appears on the picker and unsupported-route recovery screens. Approve the revised design or request changes. The neutral name “Seguro de auto” and Spanish shell copy remain design proposals.
| US-03 confirmation · concept | [Desktop](wireframes/05-confirmation-desktop.svg) | [Mobile](wireframes/05-confirmation-mobile.svg) | Explain the simulation outcome and make the quote reference easy to find and copy. Confirmation is the completion of step 3. |

### Status variants

| View | Desktop | Mobile | Trigger and recovery |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Unsupported country | [Desktop](wireframes/06-country-unsupported-desktop.svg) | [Mobile](wireframes/06-country-unsupported-mobile.svg) | Keep the attempted route and offer links to Colombia and Chile. Initial selection without a country uses the standard selector without an error. |
| Form retrieval | [Desktop](wireframes/07-loading-desktop.svg) | [Mobile](wireframes/07-loading-mobile.svg) | Initial request, reload, country change, or retry. Announce loading and withhold inputs and progression until the selected configuration is ready. |
| Unavailable or invalid form | [Desktop](wireframes/08-unavailable-desktop.svg) | [Mobile](wireframes/08-unavailable-mobile.svg) | Includes network failure, empty publication, malformed definitions, and required selects with no valid options. Display a local message and Retry. Keep the affected country's drafts in browser state. |
| Invalid details | [Desktop](wireframes/09-details-validation-desktop.svg) | [Mobile](wireframes/09-details-validation-mobile.svg) | Illustrates a failed Continue, first-invalid focus, per-field messages, age and year boundaries, and a required select with valid choices still unselected. |
| No available plans · concept | [Desktop](wireframes/10-no-plans-desktop.svg) | [Mobile](wireframes/10-no-plans-mobile.svg) | No active published plans for the current country. Explain the empty list and offer Back to details. |
| Processing simulation · concept | [Desktop](wireframes/11-payment-processing-desktop.svg) | [Mobile](wireframes/11-payment-processing-mobile.svg) | Announce processing and show the locked action. The summary and consent remain in quote state. |
| Failed simulation · concept | [Desktop](wireframes/12-payment-retry-desktop.svg) | [Mobile](wireframes/12-payment-retry-mobile.svg) | Announce failure and offer retry without asking the user to re-enter the quote. |

## Interaction annotations

1. **Country.** At the root, the country tiles are links to canonical `/co/quote/details` and `/cl/quote/details`. They are identifiable by country name and ISO code. The selector and unsupported-route recovery expose the supported country links. The URL is the source of truth during the wizard, including when the user navigates Back or Forward. Opening a different country triggers a fresh read and restores only that country’s draft when available. The original country can be revisited in the same tab via its route.
2. **Ready details.** Example fields include text identity and plate, date, numeric year, select and Boolean checkbox. Colombia's document type and placa and Chile's RUT and patente represent one possible published configuration. The order in each example is illustrative. Take the real field sequence, labels, helper text and rules from Strapi. Center the progress track and active step lane on desktop. Arrange the same field sequence row by row in the wide lane and in one column on narrow screens. Continue leads to the configured US-01 handoff and Back restores compatible values. Real plan selection is future work.
3. **Validation.** The initial placeholder in a required select announces a choice is needed without an initial error. An invalid blur displays that field's first applicable configured message. A touched value is rechecked as it changes. An unsuccessful Continue evaluates the whole form, keeps the user in place, and focuses the first invalid control in DOM order. Use an accessible message association, a visible focus outline, and a single current error per field. Avoid announcing the same message again when focusing it. Age and year messages in the frame are illustrative.
4. **Loading and recovery.** On retrieval or refresh, the shell remains while the active URL country’s fields are unavailable. The same generic recovery panel handles the invalid and no-publication cases. Retry reloads the active country's content, does not use a stale or different-country form, and reconciles by stable ID on success. Recheck the form and block progression if a retained value no longer validates or a new required field is empty. Focus the new main heading on explicit route changes. After an in-place retry, announce the result and place focus on the restored form heading if Retry was removed. Keep focus visible if a repeated failure retains Retry.
5. **Plan comparison concept.** Use one native radio group. The option's accessible name includes its plan name, with the price and concise coverage and benefits available in the same choice. Mobile stacks options in published order. The recommended tag does not choose for the user. Only a chosen plan proceeds to the summary. Price cadence and example coverage names are for later specification.
6. **Summary and consent concept.** Group policyholder and vehicle values with a nearby Edit link. Mask the document value in both rendered and assistive-technology text. Show selected plan and final price in the selected country's currency. The terms affordance can expand an inline section for current country terms. Place the native checkbox before Simular pago. Show why the action is unavailable until checked. Concepts use no real payment forms or card inputs. Processing locks repeated activation, failure preserves details and offers retry, and success shows one fictitious quote number under the same country.

Future steps use the same country and progress shell. Accessible loading and empty status placement, source-labeled content, and language are consistent across frames. The later payment status frames isolate the changed panel for review. A complete later-flow screen can keep the review context around it under its own approval.

## US-01 design traceability

| Acceptance criteria | Wireframe or annotation |
| --- | --- |
| AC-US01-01, AC-US01-07, AC-US01-09, AC-US01-12, AC-US01-15 | Both country details examples and annotation 2. Strapi owns the labels, control set and sequence. Stable IDs, typed value shapes and updates are verified once implemented. |
| AC-US01-02, AC-US01-03, AC-US01-04, AC-US01-16 | Ready, invalid and unavailable frames plus annotations 2–4. See focus, configured messaging, age/year and the distinction between an unselected select and an invalid configuration. |
| AC-US01-05, AC-US01-08, AC-US01-14 | Loading and unavailable variants, plus annotation 4 for fresh reads, quote retention and recovery reconciliation. |
| AC-US01-06 | Details and future plan back link, plus annotation 2. Verify the production US-01 handoff restores values before exercising the later screens. |
| AC-US01-10 | All responsive pairs and the [layout and component guidance](US-01-design-system.md#layout-and-order). Verify target size, focus order, reflow, accessible names and keyboard completion in the application. |
| AC-US01-11, AC-US01-13 | Standard and unsupported country selection plus annotation 1. Verify URL normalization and state isolation in the browser. |

## Review decisions

- Review the centered desktop steps and blue primary actions. The picker and unsupported-route recovery remain available for country selection.
- Confirm the document-like density, including a two-column desktop field layout and one-column mobile layout.
- Confirm the proposed Spanish shell labels and messages. Country-specific fields, labels, options, validations and product copy remain supplied by Strapi.
- Review later concepts for continuity. Their step behavior, quote calculations, consent, and simulation details remain subject to US-02 and US-03 specifications and approval.

**Approved inputs** [US-01](../../spec/US-01.md), [technology stack](../architecture/US-01-technology-stack.md), [country routing](../adr/ADR-001-multi-country-content.md), [dynamic form](../adr/ADR-002-dynamic-form-contract.md), and [wizard state](../adr/ADR-003-frontend-quote-state.md)

## Direction

A driver should be able to tell which country governs the quote, what information to supply, and what they can do next. Treat each step as part of one readable quote document. The global header carries the product identity. The progress track leads directly into the step content. On desktop, center the track and the active step composition. The country picker and URL establish the country, and each step shows the relevant business content for that country. Price and quote reference get strong typographic emphasis where they become a purchase decision or receipt.

White policy paper, pale blue tint, dark ink and the red print of a correction inform the palette. Use flat layers, simple document rules, and a single blue primary action. Georgia gives screen titles and milestones the rhythm of a document. Platform sans-serif keeps labels, entry fields and values easy to scan. The visual language is shared. Actual terminology and business content identify each country.

The review and plan patterns draw on GOV.UK's check-answers design and native radio grouping, with step-specific edit links and prices next to plan choices. [GOV.UK check answers](https://design-system.service.gov.uk/patterns/check-answers/), [GOV.UK radios](https://design-system.service.gov.uk/components/radios/)

## Foundations

Map the proposed tokens to the approved Tailwind CSS 4 theme during implementation. Use the colors on opaque surfaces.

| Token | Value and use |
| --- | --- |
| `surface-canvas` | `#F5F7FC` · background |
| `surface-panel` | `#FFFFFF` · controls, cards, header and focus gap |
| `surface-context` | `#EAF0FF` · selected plan and price block |
| `text-primary` | `#15243B` · headings, labels and values |
| `text-secondary` | `#344763` · explanatory copy |
| `text-muted` | `#405575` · help, placeholders and inactive progress labels |
| `action-primary` | `#2E6DF6` · primary and current-step fills with white foreground |
| `action-hover` | `#215BCC` · hovered or pressed primary fill |
| `action-inline` | `#1748AF` · inline links, emphasized blue text, and selected borders |
| `border-control` | `#586D91` · input, radio and checkbox outlines |
| `border-divider` | `#CCD8EE` · decorative rules |
| `focus-ring` | `#1746B4` · 2 px keyboard outline with 2 px offset. Preserve a white gap around saturated controls. |
| `intent-error` / `surface-error` | `#9E2F26` / `#FFF2EF` · invalid control, error text and recoverable panel |
| `intent-success` / `surface-success` | `#1F5B39` / `#E8F5EC` · success wording and icon |
| `surface-disabled` | `#E0E7F4` · disabled payment before consent and during processing |

| Foreground and background | Calculated contrast |
| --- | --- |
| Primary text on paper / canvas | 15.59:1 / 14.54:1 |
| Secondary text on paper / canvas | 9.43:1 / 8.80:1 |
| Muted text on paper / canvas / disabled fill | 7.57:1 / 7.06:1 / 6.09:1 |
| White text on primary / hovered primary | 4.53:1 / 6.12:1 |
| Inline action on paper / canvas / context tint | 8.13:1 / 7.59:1 / 7.13:1 |
| Control outline on paper / canvas | 5.24:1 / 4.88:1 |
| Focus outline on paper / canvas / context tint | 8.17:1 / 7.62:1 / 7.16:1 |
| Error on paper / error tint | 7.27:1 / 6.65:1 |
| Success on success tint | 7.16:1 |

Contrast uses WCAG relative luminance. Normal text targets at least 4.5:1 and essential control outlines or state indicators at least 3:1 against their surroundings. Use opaque primary blue with a white foreground and the darker inline blue for text on tinted surfaces. Messages and checked states carry meaning alongside color. [Text contrast](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/contrast-minimum.html), [Non-text contrast](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/non-text-contrast.html)

| Scale | Proposed use |
| --- | --- |
| Page title | Georgia 48/56 px wide, 32/40 px compact, normal weight |
| Section title | Georgia 28/36 px wide, 22/30 px compact, normal weight |
| Receipt number or price | System sans 28/36 px, 700, tabular numerals |
| Default body / input | System sans 16/24 px, 400 |
| Control label / button | System sans 15/20 px, 700, sentence case |
| Help / inline feedback | System sans 14/20 px, 400 for help and 700 for feedback |
| Spacing | 4, 8, 12, 16, 20, 24, 32, 40, 48 and 56 px. Use 8 px within a field, 20–24 px between fields, and 32–48 px between surfaces. |
| Shapes | 6 px controls, 8 px panels, 10 px receipt. Use tonal layers and borders. |
| Targets | At least 44 px for controls and padded link hit zones. The primary action is 48 px high. |
| Motion | At most 120 ms on fill or border changes. Reduced motion uses instant states and a static loading cue. |

## Layout and order

| Viewport | Layout |
| --- | --- |
| Compact, below 48 rem | Four-column shell with 16–20 px side padding. Fields span the content in published order. Use a compact three-label progress row. Allow copy to grow vertically. |
| Medium, 48–63.99 rem | Center one main flow. Pair consecutive fields where each gets at least 16 rem. Ancillary content follows its related block. |
| Wide, from 64 rem | Center the progress track, titles, and active step. Cap the main form and plan lane at 44.5 rem. Use a centered 58 rem composition for the summary’s paired review and price panels. Keep fields and reading text aligned to the start of their lanes. Fill the two form tracks row by row in DOM order. |

Keep the same reading order at every width and country. Labels, help, validation messages, prices and country links need room to wrap. Keep focus and errors fully visible. Verify vertical reflow at 320 CSS px and 400% zoom. The 390 px and 1200 px wireframes are review samples. [WCAG reflow](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/reflow.html), [WCAG target size](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/target-size-minimum.html)

## Components and states

| Pattern | Design contract |
| --- | --- |
| Header and country selection | The global header shows product identity. The picker and recovery for unsupported routes offer links to supported countries. The URL sets the active country and its isolated quote state. Include a main landmark, skip link and unique heading. On wizard navigation, focus the new screen heading. |
| Progress track | An informational ordered list of Datos, Plan and Resumen, centered on desktop. Mark the current step with `aria-current="step"` and expose completed status as text to assistive technology. Use separate Back and Edit actions. |
| Field | Use a visible programmatically associated label. Explain the required marker and expose requiredness natively. Use native inputs, select and checkbox. Associate help and the visible error with stable `aria-describedby` IDs. |
| Field feedback | Neutral on initial render. Show the configured error on invalid blur or unsuccessful Continue. Update or clear it as touched values change. Set `aria-invalid` while showing the error and move focus to the first invalid field on Continue. |
| Required select | Start on an unselectable placeholder with valid options waiting for a choice. After blur or Continue, show the configured required error. A required select without valid options uses the unavailable-form state. |
| Buttons and links | Buttons handle Continue, Retry and Simulate. Links handle Back and Edit. Continue remains operable in a ready invalid form. Payment is disabled before consent and during processing, with an adjacent explanation or status. |
| Loading and failure | Announce a concise polite status during retrieval. Use decorative placeholders while reading configuration for the active URL country. For missing, invalid, or failed configuration, replace the fields with a recoverable message and retry. |
| Plans | Later concept uses a native radio group with a visible legend. Recommendation and checked status have separate indicators. Keep local price, coverage and benefits close to the option. |
| Summary and receipt | Later concept uses a readable definition list and contextual edit links. Apply partial document masking to visible and spoken values. Terms and consent precede payment. Success wording accompanies a selectable quote reference. |
| Icons | Use individual local Tabler SVGs with the upstream notice. Decorative icons stay hidden from assistive technology. The shield in these frames is schematic. |

Use Spanish as the demo shell language. Keep the design notes in English and change local language attributes only for content that needs them. No static example substitutes for published Strapi business copy. [WCAG 2.2](https://www.w3.org/TR/WCAG22/), [W3C form notifications](https://www.w3.org/WAI/tutorials/forms/notifications/)

## Review and verification

The design check covers contrast, SVG accessible names, hierarchy, reading order and example wrapping. At implementation, verify both countries with keyboard and screen reader, invalid Continue, long Strapi fixtures, retry announcement, zoom, touch bounds and visible focus. Use automated accessibility checks and browser assertions alongside manual assistive-technology testing. [Wireframes and criteria map](US-01-wireframes.md)

The review draft incorporates the requested centered desktop steps and primary blue. Country selection appears on the picker and unsupported-route recovery screens. Approve the revised design or request changes. The neutral name “Seguro de auto” and Spanish shell copy remain design proposals.
| US-03 confirmation · concept | [Desktop](wireframes/05-confirmation-desktop.svg) | [Mobile](wireframes/05-confirmation-mobile.svg) | Explain the simulation outcome and make the quote reference easy to find and copy. Confirmation is the completion of step 3. |

### Status variants

| View | Desktop | Mobile | Trigger and recovery |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Unsupported country | [Desktop](wireframes/06-country-unsupported-desktop.svg) | [Mobile](wireframes/06-country-unsupported-mobile.svg) | Keep the attempted route and offer links to Colombia and Chile. Initial selection without a country uses the standard selector without an error. |
| Form retrieval | [Desktop](wireframes/07-loading-desktop.svg) | [Mobile](wireframes/07-loading-mobile.svg) | Initial request, reload, country change, or retry. Announce loading and withhold inputs and progression until the selected configuration is ready. |
| Unavailable or invalid form | [Desktop](wireframes/08-unavailable-desktop.svg) | [Mobile](wireframes/08-unavailable-mobile.svg) | Includes network failure, empty publication, malformed definitions, and required selects with no valid options. Display a local message and Retry. Keep the affected country's drafts in browser state. |
| Invalid details | [Desktop](wireframes/09-details-validation-desktop.svg) | [Mobile](wireframes/09-details-validation-mobile.svg) | Illustrates a failed Continue, first-invalid focus, per-field messages, age and year boundaries, and a required select with valid choices still unselected. |
| No available plans · concept | [Desktop](wireframes/10-no-plans-desktop.svg) | [Mobile](wireframes/10-no-plans-mobile.svg) | No active published plans for the current country. Explain the empty list and offer Back to details. |
| Processing simulation · concept | [Desktop](wireframes/11-payment-processing-desktop.svg) | [Mobile](wireframes/11-payment-processing-mobile.svg) | Announce processing and show the locked action. The summary and consent remain in quote state. |
| Failed simulation · concept | [Desktop](wireframes/12-payment-retry-desktop.svg) | [Mobile](wireframes/12-payment-retry-mobile.svg) | Announce failure and offer retry without asking the user to re-enter the quote. |

## Interaction annotations

1. **Country.** At the root, the country tiles are links to canonical `/co/quote/details` and `/cl/quote/details`. They are identifiable by country name and ISO code. The selector and unsupported-route recovery expose the supported country links. The URL is the source of truth during the wizard, including when the user navigates Back or Forward. Opening a different country triggers a fresh read and restores only that country’s draft when available. The original country can be revisited in the same tab via its route.
2. **Ready details.** Example fields include text identity and plate, date, numeric year, select and Boolean checkbox. Colombia's document type and placa and Chile's RUT and patente represent one possible published configuration. The order in each example is illustrative. Take the real field sequence, labels, helper text and rules from Strapi. Center the progress track and active step lane on desktop. Arrange the same field sequence row by row in the wide lane and in one column on narrow screens. Continue leads to the configured US-01 handoff and Back restores compatible values. Real plan selection is future work.
3. **Validation.** The initial placeholder in a required select announces a choice is needed without an initial error. An invalid blur displays that field's first applicable configured message. A touched value is rechecked as it changes. An unsuccessful Continue evaluates the whole form, keeps the user in place, and focuses the first invalid control in DOM order. Use an accessible message association, a visible focus outline, and a single current error per field. Avoid announcing the same message again when focusing it. Age and year messages in the frame are illustrative.
4. **Loading and recovery.** On retrieval or refresh, the shell remains while the active URL country’s fields are unavailable. The same generic recovery panel handles the invalid and no-publication cases. Retry reloads the active country's content, does not use a stale or different-country form, and reconciles by stable ID on success. Recheck the form and block progression if a retained value no longer validates or a new required field is empty. Focus the new main heading on explicit route changes. After an in-place retry, announce the result and place focus on the restored form heading if Retry was removed. Keep focus visible if a repeated failure retains Retry.
5. **Plan comparison concept.** Use one native radio group. The option's accessible name includes its plan name, with the price and concise coverage and benefits available in the same choice. Mobile stacks options in published order. The recommended tag does not choose for the user. Only a chosen plan proceeds to the summary. Price cadence and example coverage names are for later specification.
6. **Summary and consent concept.** Group policyholder and vehicle values with a nearby Edit link. Mask the document value in both rendered and assistive-technology text. Show selected plan and final price in the selected country's currency. The terms affordance can expand an inline section for current country terms. Place the native checkbox before Simular pago. Show why the action is unavailable until checked. Concepts use no real payment forms or card inputs. Processing locks repeated activation, failure preserves details and offers retry, and success shows one fictitious quote number under the same country.

Future steps use the same country and progress shell. Accessible loading and empty status placement, source-labeled content, and language are consistent across frames. The later payment status frames isolate the changed panel for review. A complete later-flow screen can keep the review context around it under its own approval.

## US-01 design traceability

| Acceptance criteria | Wireframe or annotation |
| --- | --- |
| AC-US01-01, AC-US01-07, AC-US01-09, AC-US01-12, AC-US01-15 | Both country details examples and annotation 2. Strapi owns the labels, control set and sequence. Stable IDs, typed value shapes and updates are verified once implemented. |
| AC-US01-02, AC-US01-03, AC-US01-04, AC-US01-16 | Ready, invalid and unavailable frames plus annotations 2–4. See focus, configured messaging, age/year and the distinction between an unselected select and an invalid configuration. |
| AC-US01-05, AC-US01-08, AC-US01-14 | Loading and unavailable variants, plus annotation 4 for fresh reads, quote retention and recovery reconciliation. |
| AC-US01-06 | Details and future plan back link, plus annotation 2. Verify the production US-01 handoff restores values before exercising the later screens. |
| AC-US01-10 | All responsive pairs and the [layout and component guidance](US-01-design-system.md#layout-and-order). Verify target size, focus order, reflow, accessible names and keyboard completion in the application. |
| AC-US01-11, AC-US01-13 | Standard and unsupported country selection plus annotation 1. Verify URL normalization and state isolation in the browser. |

## Review decisions

- Review the centered desktop steps and blue primary actions. The picker and unsupported-route recovery remain available for country selection.
- Confirm the document-like density, including a two-column desktop field layout and one-column mobile layout.
- Confirm the proposed Spanish shell labels and messages. Country-specific fields, labels, options, validations and product copy remain supplied by Strapi.
- Review later concepts for continuity. Their step behavior, quote calculations, consent, and simulation details remain subject to US-02 and US-03 specifications and approval.

*** Add File: docs/design/US-02-plan-selection.md
+# US-02 — Plan selection design
+
+**Status** Proposed · Pending human approval  
+**Basis** [Approved US-02 specification](../../spec/US-02.md), [ADR-004](../adr/ADR-004-plan-catalog-and-selection.md), and the [shared design system](US-01-design-system.md)
+
+## Compare and choose
+
+Keep the product-only header, centered wizard track, and centered Plans lane. Mark Datos complete and Plan current. Use **Elige tu plan** as the step heading and **Planes disponibles** as the visible group legend. Cards follow the published order. Pair consecutive cards across the wide lane and stack them in one column below the wide breakpoint. Match reading and focus order at every width. Let names, prices and lists wrap and grow vertically.
+
+| Review specimen | Annotations |
+| --- | --- |
+| [Desktop comparison, Colombia](wireframes/US-02-plans-comparison-desktop.svg) | Esencial is checked and Ruta is recommended. The card separates short description, coverages and benefits. |
+| [Existing mobile concept, Chile](wireframes/03-plans-mobile.svg) | Reuse the stacked layout. Apply the same card hierarchy as the desktop comparison and the price and action order below. |
+| [Existing empty desktop](wireframes/10-no-plans-desktop.svg) · [mobile](wireframes/10-no-plans-mobile.svg) | Reuse the empty panel and **Volver a datos** action. Substitute the active country's name in the message. |
+
+Lead each card with the radio and plan name, followed by the price and the short description. Show the published entries under **Coberturas** and **Beneficios**, omitting a heading if its list is empty. Use one final price from Strapi. Show the explicit currency code and local separators with \`es-CO\` and two fractional digits or \`es-CL\` and zero fractional digits. Examples are **COP 129.900,50** and **CLP 24.900**. Example amounts and plan copy are fictitious. Display the actual published plan content as plain text. Payment cadence is outside the current price contract.
+
+Use native radios with a common group name inside a fieldset. Give each radio an explicit label containing its visible plan name. Associate its price and any **Recomendado** text as a description. Keep long coverage and benefit lists as readable content in the card. The radio and label row provide a 44 px minimum target. Use the checked mark and selected border and tint for selection, and a separate text tag for a recommendation. The fieldset starts unchecked unless an earlier explicit choice is restored and revalidated. [GOV.UK radios](https://design-system.service.gov.uk/components/radios/)
+
+## States and actions
+
+| State | Presentation and next action |
+| --- | --- |
+| Ready, unselected | Keep **Continuar** visibly disabled and place **Selecciona un plan para continuar** next to it. Offer **Volver a datos**. |
+| Ready, selected | Enable **Continuar** when the current eligible choice and Details are valid. Selecting a different radio replaces the choice in place. Render Back before Continue in the visual and keyboard sequence. Stack actions on compact screens and use a full-width primary action. |
+| Loading or retrying | Keep the Plans shell with **Cargando los planes…** and the shared [loading treatment](wireframes/07-loading-desktop.svg). Withhold cards and progression. Any placeholders are decorative and static with reduced motion. Keep Back available. |
+| Revalidating before handoff | Keep Plan as the current step until the read succeeds. Show **Verificando tu plan…** in the same status area, with plan choices and further Continue activation unavailable. Back returns to Details and supersedes the read. |
+| Empty | Show **No hay planes disponibles** and **Por ahora no hay planes para [país].** Offer Back. |
+| Unavailable | Adapt the [shared recovery treatment](wireframes/08-unavailable-desktop.svg) with **Planes no disponibles**, **No pudimos cargar los planes. Intenta de nuevo.**, **Reintentar**, and Back. Keep progression blocked during retry and show only current results. |
+| Reselection required | When a successful refresh removes or reprices the chosen plan, show the current choices unchecked and the message **Tu plan cambió o ya no está disponible. Selecciona un plan para continuar.** If no plans remain, use the empty state and explain the lost choice without instructing the user to choose. |
+
+**Volver a datos** links to the same country's Details and leaves the draft intact. A valid unchanged selection can be restored after a fresh read. **Continuar** reaches the same-country Summary handoff only after successful revalidation. Use the existing step-navigation convention at the handoff. US-03 owns the summary content.
+
+## Keyboard, focus and announcements
+
+- Preserve native radio interaction. Tab and Shift+Tab enter and leave the group, arrows move and choose within it, and Space checks the focused choice. Keep focus on the radio after a choice. Use the shared visible focus ring and preserve the browser's checked mark in forced colors.
+- Focus the step heading on route entry. If an activated control disappears during revalidation, move focus to the persistent step heading. When retry replaces its control with current results, return focus to the Plans heading. If a retry fails in place, retain focus on Retry. A user who moved focus to Back while waiting keeps it there.
+- Use one polite status region for meaningful asynchronous changes, including loading, verification, successful retry and reselection. When moving focus to a recovery heading, let that focus movement communicate the recovery instead of announcing the same text twice. Native checked state conveys the radio change. [WCAG status messages](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/status-messages.html)
+
+## Design review coverage
+
+| Criteria | Review and later verification |
+| --- | --- |
+| AC-US02-01, AC-US02-02 | Confirm published order, copy placement and both price formats. Verify with long content and empty coverage or benefit lists. |
+| AC-US02-03, AC-US02-04 | Confirm independent recommendation and selection, disabled unselected action, one checked radio, same-country Back and gated handoff. |
+| AC-US02-05, AC-US02-06 | Confirm the empty, loading, retry, revalidation and reselection treatments. Verify a repriced or withdrawn plan cannot reach the handoff. |
+| AC-US02-07 | Verify keyboard and accessible names and descriptions at desktop and mobile sizes, 320 CSS px reflow, 400% zoom, and focus through an unsuccessful and successful retry. |
+
+The proposal is ready for explicit design approval or requested revisions.
*** End Patch`))

# US-02 — Plan selection design

**Status** Human approved on 2026-11-22 ([approval record](../approvals/US-02-design-approval.md))  
**Basis** [Approved US-02 specification](../../spec/US-02.md), [ADR-004](../adr/ADR-004-plan-catalog-and-selection.md), and the [shared design system](US-01-design-system.md)

## Compare and choose

Keep the product-only header, centered wizard track, and centered Plans lane. Mark Datos complete and Plan current. Use **Elige tu plan** as the step heading and **Planes disponibles** as the visible group legend. Cards follow the published order. Pair consecutive cards across the wide lane and stack them in one column below the wide breakpoint. Match reading and focus order at every width. Let names, prices and lists wrap and grow vertically.

| Review specimen | Annotations |
| --- | --- |
| [Desktop comparison, Colombia](wireframes/US-02-plans-comparison-desktop.svg) | Esencial is checked and Ruta is recommended. The card separates short description, coverages and benefits. |
| [Existing mobile concept, Chile](wireframes/03-plans-mobile.svg) | Reuse the stacked layout. Apply the same card hierarchy as the desktop comparison and the price and action order below. |
| [Existing empty desktop](wireframes/10-no-plans-desktop.svg) · [mobile](wireframes/10-no-plans-mobile.svg) | Reuse the empty panel and **Volver a datos** action. Substitute the active country's name in the message. |

Lead each card with the radio and plan name, followed by the price and the short description. Show the published entries under **Coberturas** and **Beneficios**, omitting a heading if its list is empty. Use one final price from Strapi. Show the explicit currency code and local separators with `es-CO` and two fractional digits or `es-CL` and zero fractional digits. Examples are **COP 129.900,50** and **CLP 24.900**. Example amounts and plan copy are fictitious. Display the actual published plan content as plain text. Payment cadence is outside the current price contract.

Use native radios with a common group name inside a fieldset. Give each radio an explicit label containing its visible plan name. Associate its price and any **Recomendado** text as a description. Keep long coverage and benefit lists as readable content in the card. The radio and label row provide a 44 px minimum target. Use the checked mark and selected border and tint for selection, and a separate text tag for a recommendation. The fieldset starts unchecked unless an earlier explicit choice is restored and revalidated. [GOV.UK radios](https://design-system.service.gov.uk/components/radios/)

## States and actions

| State | Presentation and next action |
| --- | --- |
| Ready, unselected | Keep **Continuar** visibly disabled and place **Selecciona un plan para continuar** next to it. Offer **Volver a datos**. |
| Ready, selected | Enable **Continuar** when the current eligible choice and Details are valid. Selecting a different radio replaces the choice in place. Render Back before Continue in the visual and keyboard sequence. Stack actions on compact screens and use a full-width primary action. |
| Loading or retrying | Keep the Plans shell with **Cargando los planes…** and the shared [loading treatment](wireframes/07-loading-desktop.svg). Withhold cards and progression. Any placeholders are decorative and static with reduced motion. Keep Back available. |
| Revalidating before handoff | Keep Plan as the current step until the read succeeds. Show **Verificando tu plan…** in the same status area, with plan choices and further Continue activation unavailable. Back returns to Details and supersedes the read. |
| Empty | Show **No hay planes disponibles** and **Por ahora no hay planes para [país].** Offer Back. |
| Unavailable | Adapt the [shared recovery treatment](wireframes/08-unavailable-desktop.svg) with **Planes no disponibles**, **No pudimos cargar los planes. Intenta de nuevo.**, **Reintentar**, and Back. Keep progression blocked during retry and show only current results. |
| Reselection required | When a successful refresh removes or reprices the chosen plan, show the current choices unchecked and the message **Tu plan cambió o ya no está disponible. Selecciona un plan para continuar.** If no plans remain, use the empty state and explain the lost choice without instructing the user to choose. |

**Volver a datos** links to the same country's Details and leaves the draft intact. A valid unchanged selection can be restored after a fresh read. **Continuar** reaches the same-country Summary handoff only after successful revalidation. Use the existing step-navigation convention at the handoff. US-03 owns the summary content.

## Keyboard, focus and announcements

- Preserve native radio interaction. Tab and Shift+Tab enter and leave the group, arrows move and choose within it, and Space checks the focused choice. Keep focus on the radio after a choice. Use the shared visible focus ring and preserve the browser's checked mark in forced colors.
- Focus the step heading on route entry. If an activated control disappears during revalidation, move focus to the persistent step heading. When retry replaces its control with current results, return focus to the Plans heading. If a retry fails in place, retain focus on Retry. A user who moved focus to Back while waiting keeps it there.
- Use one polite status region for meaningful asynchronous changes, including loading, verification, successful retry and reselection. When moving focus to a recovery heading, let that focus movement communicate the recovery instead of announcing the same text twice. Native checked state conveys the radio change. [WCAG status messages](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/status-messages.html)

## Design review coverage

| Criteria | Review and later verification |
| --- | --- |
| AC-US02-01, AC-US02-02 | Confirm published order, copy placement and both price formats. Verify with long content and empty coverage or benefit lists. |
| AC-US02-03, AC-US02-04 | Confirm independent recommendation and selection, disabled unselected action, one checked radio, same-country Back and gated handoff. |
| AC-US02-05, AC-US02-06 | Confirm the empty, loading, retry, revalidation and reselection treatments. Verify a repriced or withdrawn plan cannot reach the handoff. |
| AC-US02-07 | Verify keyboard and accessible names and descriptions at desktop and mobile sizes, 320 CSS px reflow, 400% zoom, and focus through an unsuccessful and successful retry. |

The project owner approved the design on 2026-11-22.
68:| Compact, below 48 rem | Four-column shell with 16–20 px side padding. Fields span the content in published order. Use a compact three-label progress row. Allow copy to grow vertically. |
70:| Wide, from 64 rem | Center the progress track, titles, and active step. Cap the main form and plan lane at 44.5 rem. Use a centered 58 rem composition for the summary’s paired review and price panels. Keep fields and reading text aligned to the start of their lanes. Fill the two form tracks row by row in DOM order. |

# US-02 — Plan card layout and selection revision

**Status** Proposed · Pending human approval  
**Basis** [Approved US-02 design](US-02-plan-selection.md), [US-02 specification](../../spec/US-02.md), and [ADR-004](../adr/ADR-004-plan-catalog-and-selection.md)

## Plan card layout

Set the centered Plans lane to a maximum of 58 rem. Base the card grid on the lane's available inline width after shell padding. Use 16 rem minimum tracks, 1.5 rem gaps, and one to three columns. Allow a single track to shrink below 16 rem when using a narrower lane.

| Available lane width | Capacity |
| --- | --- |
| Below 33.5 rem | One card per row |
| 33.5 rem up to 51 rem | Two cards per row |
| 51 rem and above | Three cards per row |

Keep Esencial, Ruta and Integral together in one row at the widest size. Use the same rules for any published catalog size, collapse unused columns when the catalog is smaller, and place additional plans on the next row in published order. Match reading and keyboard order at every width. Reuse the existing card hierarchy and spacing, allow long plan names, prices, and list items to wrap, and let cards grow vertically. Test reflow without horizontal scrolling at 320 CSS px and the equivalent 400% zoom. [CSS Grid track repetition](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-grid/#auto-repeat) · [WCAG reflow](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/reflow.html)

## Whole-card selection

A click or tap anywhere within a ready card selects its plan. Keep one native radio per card in the existing fieldset, and associate the visible plan name with its radio through an explicit `label`. Stretch that label's transparent pointer target across the card. Keep the actual radio directly operable and the coverage and benefit lists in the reading order. Associate the formatted price and, when present, the **Recomendado** tag with the radio through `aria-describedby`. The card has a single selectable control and a single accessible name.

Preserve native Tab, arrow key and Space behavior and the visible checked indicator. Show the shared focus outline for keyboard focus and keep it visible in forced colors. Selection updates the checked state and card emphasis in place without shifting the layout. Selecting a card leaves the user on Plans and makes **Continuar** available when the quote can progress. [HTML label element](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/forms.html#the-label-element) · [Radio group keyboard interaction](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/radio/)

## Design review checks

- **AC-US02-01 and AC-US02-07.** Confirm all three seeded cards appear in order in a single row when 51 rem is available. Check just below and at 33.5 rem and 51 rem, plus compact reflow with long CMS content.
- **AC-US02-03, AC-US02-04 and AC-US02-07.** Click or tap the radio, plan title, price, list text and card padding. Each hit selects that plan, replaces any prior choice and keeps recommendation distinct. Confirm the group exposes one radio per plan with name, description and checked state, and can be operated by keyboard.
